issue: Under the safety-valve provision, does a defendant become ineligible for relief if he has any one of the three listed criminal-history features (more than 4 points, a prior 3-point offense, or a prior 2-point violent offense), or only if he has all three?

sides.position: The "and" in § 3553(f)(1) is conjunctive, so a defendant is disqualified from safety-valve relief only if he possesses all three criminal-history criteria.
cases: United States v. Lopez, 998 F.3d 431 (9th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Garcon, 54 F.4th 1274 (11th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: A defendant who possesses any one of the three specified criminal-history criteria is disqualified from safety-valve relief, whether the "and" is read as disjunctive or as conjunctive but distributive.
cases: United States v. Palomares, 52 F.4th 640 (5th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Pulsifer, 39 F.4th 1018 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Pace, 48 F.4th 741 (7th Cir. 2022)

this_court: Adopts the conjunctive reading: a defendant must possess all three criteria to be disqualified, siding with the Ninth Circuit.
quote: A circuit split now exists on this issue.
cite: United States v. Julian Garcon, 54 F.4th 1274 (11th Cir. 2022)
